nodes.label: Footer Legal Credential Line
nodes.rationale: Every number reads from the Customizer and is omitted when unset, because on a site whose central argument is 'go and verify our registration', one number that does not check out discredits the rest.

nodes.label: IATA Licence Number Omitted
nodes.rationale: The old footer printed 'IATA License: TK92456' on every page. IATA accreditation is for airline ticketing agents, which this business is not, so an unverifiable number was undermining the verification argument. Removed; if genuine it belongs in the Customizer with the others.

nodes.label: WhatsApp Sticky Bar (phones only)
nodes.rationale: Standard and effective for this market on phones, but on desktop it fights the calm the rest of the page is built on, so it is phone-only.

nodes.label: Tradition Doors Before Prices
nodes.rationale: The tradition doors are rendered above the catalogue so they reframe what the visitor thinks they are shopping for before a price appears. Once someone is comparing $350 to $1,000 the pilgrimage framing is gone and the site competes on cost with all of Thamel.

nodes.label: Editor Prose Passthrough
nodes.rationale: Anything the editor wrote on the page itself still renders below the catalogue, so the template does not silently swallow their content.

nodes.label: Real Kora Altitude Interpolation
nodes.rationale: The altitude readout is interpolated across the real profile of the kora, so the number climbing past 5,630 at the Dolma La is the number a pilgrim actually crosses. Teaching something true is the whole justification for the interaction.

nodes.label: Hold-to-Walk Progress Drive
nodes.rationale: Progress eases back on early release rather than snapping to zero: a snap says the attempt did not count, an ease says the walk is simply not finished. Full circle takes ~4s.

nodes.label: Keyboard/AT One-Press Completion
nodes.rationale: Keyboard and assistive technology press rather than hold, so the control is a real button and a plain activation completes the circle in one go with the same payoff.

nodes.label: Reduced-Motion Handling (both directions)
nodes.rationale: Reduced motion starts completed and never animates; coming back out of reduced motion mid-session leaves the circle closed rather than making the visitor earn the payoff twice.

nodes.label: Three-State Readout Throttle
nodes.rationale: The readout is only rewritten when the state changes so a screen reader is not told the same sentence sixty times a second.

nodes.label: Estimated Total Renderer
nodes.rationale: Labelled explicitly as an estimate because the business quotes by invoice; a number that looks like a checkout figure would be a promise the operator has not made.

nodes.label: Group-Size Tier Selection (priceEach)
nodes.rationale: The applicable tier is the HIGHEST threshold the party actually reaches, not the smallest price. The headline price_from is the marketing figure and is normally the largest group's rate; getting this backwards quoted a solo pilgrim the ten-person rate, an error only discovered at invoice time.

nodes.label: Per-Person Rate Disclosed Both Directions
nodes.rationale: Whenever the effective per-person rate differs from the headline, it is stated in BOTH directions. A solo pilgrim seeing 'From $350' must be told their own rate is $650 before they enquire, not after the invoice.

nodes.label: Async Enquiry Submit
nodes.rationale: Sends without throwing away the page the visitor is reading; if no ajaxUrl is available it falls through to a native form post rather than swallowing the enquiry silently.

nodes.label: 300-Second stale-while-revalidate Ceiling
nodes.rationale: stale-while-revalidate is honoured by browsers on navigation, not only CDNs. With a long window a returning visitor gets the OLD HTML while every versioned CSS/JS URL updates normally, so the site renders the old template with the new design tokens. It survives hard refresh, curl, and fresh URLs, and cost a full debugging session once.

nodes.label: WP_CONSTANTS sprintf Value Resolver
nodes.rationale: The value is usually a sprintf %d placeholder filled from a later argument, so the checker scans the whole header call and resolves WordPress *_IN_SECONDS constants rather than reading the format string alone.

nodes.label: PHP Structure Sanity Checker
nodes.rationale: Not a parser and not a replacement for bin/lint-php.sh: it exists so brace/quote/heredoc errors introduced while generating PHP are caught when no PHP binary is available.

nodes.label: PHP Code Region Isolation
nodes.rationale: Theme files flip between PHP and raw output many times and the HTML/CSS halves are full of braces that are just text; checking those produced a wall of false positives on the widget files.

nodes.label: String-Aware ?> Finder
nodes.rationale: inc/sitemap.php builds XML containing '<?xml ... ?>' inside a single-quoted string; a naive search treated that as the end of PHP mode and reported a bogus unclosed brace. Comments are skipped first so an apostrophe in a // comment does not read as a string open.

nodes.label: Semantic Content Wrapper (the_content, prio 20)
nodes.rationale: Skips wrapping for Elementor-built pages (detected via non-empty _elementor_data) because those handle their own structure. Note: it computes an $itemtype per post type but never emits it.

nodes.label: Publish-Status and Password Guard
nodes.rationale: The endpoint is public (permission_callback => __return_true) and previously checked post_type but not post_status, so anyone could walk IDs and read draft, pending, private and password-protected packages including body, pricing and meta. The guard returns the SAME 404 as a missing package so the response cannot confirm that an unpublished package exists at an ID.

nodes.label: tk_section_head() Section Heading
nodes.rationale: A section heading is one call rather than three elements someone can forget to pair. The brass rule under every heading is the system's single ornament and is what makes the page read as one continuous walk rather than stacked sections.

nodes.label: tk_tradition_count() (1-hour transient)
nodes.rationale: Door counts are computed, not typed, because typed counts go stale the first time a package is added. Cached for an hour because it runs three times per homepage load and changes about once a season.

nodes.label: tk_flush_tradition_counts() Invalidation
nodes.rationale: Without invalidation the doors show yesterday's numbers for an hour after publishing, which is exactly when the editor looks at the site to check.

nodes.label: tk_tradition_geometry() Four Tradition Marks
nodes.rationale: Four genuinely different figures (torana, dharma wheel, shaligram, yantra), not one glyph recoloured, because recolouring one mark would claim these are four flavours of the same thing - the one claim this site must not make.

nodes.label: tk_default_nav() Fallback Navigation
nodes.rationale: The live menu carried only two links and About/Contact existed as pages but were never added. A fallback listing the site's real pages means navigation is never poorer than the site itself, whatever was configured in admin.

nodes.label: Deity Hero Inline Navbar
nodes.rationale: Hard-codes /sacred-paths, /yatra-packages, /about and /contact, which do not match the /about-us and /contact-us URLs the theme's own fallback nav and footer use.

nodes.label: Package Card Template Part
nodes.rationale: The old card laid a dark band across the bottom of the photo with the title inside; it was flagged on every card because the band had no relationship to the image, cutting it at an arbitrary line and changing height with the title. Now the photo is edge to edge and nothing overlaps. Every card is structurally identical, and a package with no thumbnail gets a drawn placeholder rather than a broken-image icon.

nodes.label: Before You Go Guides Section
nodes.rationale: This is the entire SEO surface: 'Muktinath yatra best time' and 'Kailash permit requirements' outrank any package name in search volume and feed the package pages. The guide post type is empty today, so four fallback cards drawn from customer research point at the enquiry form rather than rendering nothing or four dead links.

nodes.label: Check Us Before You Pay Us Section
nodes.rationale: Fraud is the number one objection in this category and it is earned - an operator took over fifteen lakh rupees from seven pilgrims and never ran the trip. A properly registered agency actively encourages verification, and both Nepali registers are public, so the section hands over the means to check rather than displaying numbers. Rows with no number are not rendered and the whole section disappears if nothing is set, because the one thing it cannot survive is a number that does not check out.

nodes.label: Money Explainer and Trust Cluster
nodes.rationale: Sits directly under the enquiry form because that is where doubt peaks: someone has just typed their details for a company in another country and the next thought is what happens to my money. Numbers come from the Customizer and are omitted when unset - a trust block showing an empty bracket does the opposite of its job.

nodes.label: Package Spec Strip
nodes.rationale: Every value comes from a field, none is typed into a layout - the fix for live-site drift where a package said 12 days in its title and 14 in its spec block, or a helicopter ride was described as a moderate trek. Rows with no value are not rendered because 'Altitude:' with nothing after it reads as a broken page.

nodes.label: Hero Accessibility Requirements
nodes.rationale: Video muted by default with an explicit sound toggle, focus states on all interactive elements, ARIA labels, and semantic h1/section/button structure.

hyperedges.label: Credential verification contract
hyperedges.description: One set of Customizer theme mods (tk_taan_number, tk_ntb_number, tk_company_reg) is rendered in three places with the same rule everywhere: omit the row when unset, never print a placeholder, and always link onward to the /#verify register list. The rule exists because a single number that does not check out discredits the whole trust argument.

hyperedges.label: pilgrimage_package meta fan-out
hyperedges.description: Five independent readers of the same pilgrimage_package post meta, split across two access styles: geo-content, the REST endpoint and the Elementor card call get_post_meta() directly (trip_length, price_from, has_lodge, has_helicopter, includes_meals, includes_rituals, key_stops), while the redesigned template parts go through the tk_package()/tk_package_has()/tk_package_grading() field API. The two halves can drift.

hyperedges.label: Scroll reveal class contract
hyperedges.description: An undeclared three-class contract: PHP emits .tk-rv on individual elements, .tk-rule on the brass hairline, and .tk-stagger on containers whose direct .tk-rv children should be revealed in sequence; reveal.js observes exactly those selectors and motion.css defines their rest and revealed states. Nothing in the PHP declares the dependency.
